newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaican government passes Air Jamaica guarantee.
newsitem.headline: Jamaican government passes Air Jamaica guarantee.

text.p: The lower house of the Jamaican parliament approved a US$54 million guarantee Tuesday for a financing package for Air Jamaica, which will allow the airline to further expand its fleet.
The guarantee was three times larger than the amount the airline originally said it was seeking earlier this year.

The guarantee covers a US$30 million loan from Jamaica's National Commercial Bank, which is also a minority shareholder in the airline, and US$24 million in fixed-rate promissory notes being issued by the airline through Citicorp's Citibank.
The package will go toward the US$164 million needed to acquire four new A320s from Airbus Industrie. The remainder is being financing through credit from Airbus.

Since it was privatized in late 1994, the airline has replaced its aging Boeing Co 727s and A300s for A310s and A320s. Air Jamaica also wet leases two MD83s for its Chicago route. Airline officials said the new fleet is needed to reduce fuel and maintenance costs and increase its ability to be profitable.

However, since it was sold to local investors, the airline has lost some US$70 million, due largely to the decision by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration to give Jamaica a Category II rating, thus restricting Air Jamaica from opening new routes.
Jamaica was informed by the FAA late last month that it had failed in its latest bid to be returned to a Category I rating.
